title: Open the project

blocks.what_we_do:
Open `GWAS_training_session.Rproj` from the extracted folder. In RStudio,
open this notebook from `lessons/`. Run commands in the console at the project root.
blocks.why:
Relative paths are interpreted from the working directory. Keeping one project
root avoids copying your personal absolute paths into every command.
blocks.you_need: The complete extracted project from 0.5, not an individual downloaded notebook.
blocks.command:
```{r s0-6_project}
getwd()
stopifnot(file.exists("config.R"), file.exists("R/course.R"))
```

Terminal equivalent: from the project directory, run
`Rscript -e "stopifnot(file.exists('config.R'))"`. `stopifnot` stops when a
required condition is false. No output means this check passed.
blocks.expected_result:
Your project folder is printed. The file checks finish without an error.
Your personal folder path will differ from the author's path.
blocks.troubleshooting:
If `config.R` is absent, reopen the project from the extracted source folder.
Do not create a blank replacement or rename a downloaded HTML page to `.R`.
blocks.quick_check:
Does a relative path starting `R/` refer to a folder on every computer's C drive?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>No. It refers to the R folder under the current project root.</details>
blocks.files_created: RStudio may create local project settings under `.Rproj.user/`; they are ignored by Git.
